latest_findings.claim: At e in [0, 0.7] (N=64, 4 layers, d_model=64, m2 in [0.1, 1]), the layer-4 accel_step best-of-5 control R2 was 0.543, 0.553 and 0.559 (seeds 72, 70, 71). That sits between the e <= 0.5 controls (0.71-0.77) and the e <= 0.85 controls (0.25-0.35). The final accel_step margins were 0.257, 0.260 and 0.241 (R2 0.80-0.81), and accel_step first stayed above the 0.1 margin at steps 60, 60 and 70. Force was much weaker: margins 0.140 (layer 4), 0.101 (layer 3) and 0.121 (layer 1), against controls of 0.27-0.39. Measured against available headroom, accel_step reached about 0.55 and force about 0.16-0.22. All expected-if-true criteria were met.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 seeds met every pre-registered criterion, and the controls (0.54-0.56) sit well inside the [0.38, 0.66] window and well away from both falsification bands (>= 0.68 or <= 0.36). Six things limit the claim. (1) This adds only one intermediate eccentricity ceiling. Three points look monotonic and close to a straight line (linear interpolation predicts about 0.49, observed 0.55), but they cannot show that the decline is smooth rather than a gentle curve. (2) The e <= 0.5 and e <= 0.85 reference values come from earlier experiments that may have used different seeds, m2 ranges or other settings, so this is not a matched one-factor sweep. (3) Only the control-R2 part of the hypothesis is clearly intermediate. The final margin (0.24-0.26) is at the low end of the e <= 0.85 regime (0.26-0.29), and formation (steps 60-70) matches the e <= 0.85 window rather than falling between 80-100 and 60-70. Margin size and formation timing therefore do not move in step with control R2. (4) Seed 72 hits exactly 0.100 at step 50, so its formation step is 50 or 60 depending on whether the bar is inclusive. Checkpoints are 10 steps apart. (5) The proposed mechanism, a^3 dominating accel_step variance, was not tested directly. No a^3 or per-system-demeaned target was probed. (6) Seed 70's force margin only reaches 0.101 at step 590, so force beating its control is marginal there. A matched sweep (e ceilings of 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8 and 0.85 with the same m2 range and seeds) that showed a step in control R2 between neighbouring ceilings would weaken the smooth-scaling reading. So would a direct a^3 probe that fails to account for the control R2.

latest_findings.claim: At N=256, e<=0.5 (seeds 65-69), accel_step crosses the 0.1 margin and stays above it at steps 100/100/100/100/125 (seeds 65/66/68/69/67, read from the trajectories), and reaches half of its final margin at steps 75/95/85/95/120. The N=64 arm for the same seeds formed at 65-90 (0.1 bar) and 40-70 (half-final), so every N=256 seed is at least +10 steps later on the 0.1 bar, with a mean delay of roughly +15 to +40; the per-seed >=+15 test could not be checked because the paired per-seed N=64 values were not available. Final accel_step R2 is 0.853-0.900 vs controls 0.685-0.726 (margins 0.162-0.175), while force ends with no margin (-0.004 to 0.051, beats_control false in all 5) after an early transient of 0.17-0.23 at steps 10-20, and no run beats the baseline (val_mse_ratio 11.8-14.2).
latest_findings.confidence_note: The direction is consistent: the earliest N=256 formation step (100) is later than the latest N=64 step for these seeds (90). The refutation pattern did not happen, because the 0.1-bar delay is >=+10 in all 5 seeds and the half-final delay can be <=+10 only for seed 65 (N=256 half-final step 75; it first crosses at 75, dips at 80, and stays above from 85). But the experiment is defined on per-seed pairs, and this analysis only had the N=64 range (65-90 / 40-70) from open-question summaries, not the per-seed values in f-20261012-054929-0067. That file was not readable here, the same failure as q-20261012-052949-98cc. Using those ranges as bounds, the pooled 11-seed mean delay is about +19.5 to +31 on the 0.1 bar (earlier deltas +20/+70/+30/0/0/+20) and about +23 or more on half-final. Both bounds straddle or barely clear the +20 criterion. Seed 68's probes_final.formed_at_step is 105, but its trajectory crosses at 100, the same one-checkpoint lag as q-20261012-032843-df65; trajectory values are used here. Joining the per-seed N=64 trajectories would most likely turn this into supported. It would stay inconclusive or flip if two or more N=64 seeds formed at 90 on the 0.1 bar. Formation at N=256 again happens while the model is about 12x worse than constant-velocity extrapolation, so it says nothing about task success.

latest_findings.claim: Refuted under the pre-registered criterion: 3 of 5 seeds fall outside the N=64 reference window, which needed at least 4 of 5 inside. Reading each seed's trajectory, accel_step forms persistently (margin stays >= 0.1 at every later checkpoint) at step 65 for seeds 67 and 68, and at step 90 for seeds 65, 66 and 69. Accel_step reaches half its final margin at steps 45, 55, 70, 55 and 40 for seeds 67, 68, 65, 66 and 69. That puts seed 67 outside both windows, seed 68 outside the [70,110] formation window and seed 69 outside the [50,100] half-final window; only seeds 65 and 66 meet both. Final accel_step margin is 0.130-0.158 in all seeds (R2 0.869-0.909 vs control 0.713-0.772), but force also beats its control at the final checkpoint in 2 of 5 seeds (seed 67: 0.526 vs 0.423, margin 0.103; seed 68: 0.579 vs 0.474, margin 0.105), against margins of 0.047-0.090 in the other three. That contradicts the 'force does not beat control' part of the prediction. All runs beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.41-0.45).
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 5 runs completed the full 300 steps, and no run is stopped or marked bad. The misses are small. Seeds 67 and 68 cross for good at step 65, one 5-step checkpoint before the window opens, and seed 69's half-final step of 40 is 10 steps early. So the result says the window was too narrow, not that N=64 timing has moved much. Overall, persistent formation spans steps 65-90 and half-final spans steps 40-70, roughly 10-20 steps earlier than the 80-100 window quoted from seeds 47-49, 56-58 and 62-64. The earlier runs used 10-step checkpoints, while these use 5-step checkpoints. That alone can pull crossings earlier by up to one older checkpoint, so part of the shift may be resolution, not a different timing. The force 'beats_control' results are borderline: margins of 0.103 and 0.105 against a 0.1 bar, with control_spread 0.034-0.048. They should not be read as a learned force representation. Every seed shows the same early force transient: margin 0.12-0.19 at steps 10-25, falling to 0.002-0.10 by steps 40-55. formed_at_step agrees with the trajectory for 4 seeds but not seed 68: it reports 80, while the margin is >= 0.1 at every checkpoint from step 65. That repeats the lag described in q-20261012-032843-df65. Persistent formation happens at val_mse_ratio 2.1-3.3 (2.7-4.3% of each run's step-0 value), which fits the absolute ~2-3 band proposed in q-20261012-044258-7e31. Two things would change this verdict: re-reading the earlier N=64 seeds at 5-step resolution and finding them at 65-90 too, or a pre-registered window of [60,100] for persistent formation and [40,80] for half-final.

latest_findings.claim: Halving lr from 0.001 to 0.0005 (N=64, e in [0, 0.85], seeds 59-61, best-of-5 controls) delays accel_step formation only slightly. Read from the trajectories, the 0.1-bar margin is first crossed and held at steps 70 (seed 59), 80 (seed 60) and 100 (seed 61), compared with 60/60/70 at lr=0.001. That is +10/+20/+30 steps rather than the roughly 2x (>= 100 in all seeds) that proportional scaling predicts. Final accel_step R2 is 0.49-0.59 at layer 4 vs controls 0.25-0.33, margin 0.244-0.257. Force never beats its control: R2 0.22-0.28 vs 0.15-0.21, margin 0.065-0.078. All runs beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.214-0.224).
latest_findings.confidence_note: The pre-registered false condition holds: 2 of 3 seeds are at step <= 90 and within 20 steps of lr=0.001. The undertraining escape does not apply, since all final margins are >= 0.24. The hypothesis's 60/60/70 baseline is assumed to belong to seeds 59/60/61. Under any assignment of those values, at least 2 seeds are still within 20 steps, so the verdict does not depend on that assumption. Lowering lr did slow training: final val_mse_ratio is about 0.22 here against about 0.13 at lr=0.001. Seed 61 (+30) is also the one seed that moved as much as predicted. So formation is not independent of lr. It shifts sub-proportionally, and the result rules out 'set by cumulative lr*steps' rather than 'unaffected by the optimizer'. Half-final-margin steps here are 100/90/110 (seeds 59/60/61). The seed-matched lr=0.001 half-final values are not in this record, so that half of the expected-if-true criterion cannot be checked here. The 10-step checkpoint spacing limits resolution to about ±10 steps. The verdict would weaken if the lr=0.001 trajectories for seeds 59-61 give formation steps of 50 or earlier, or if a lr=0.00025 arm shows formation scaling steeply. probes_final.formed_at_step matches the trajectory in all 3 runs, so there is no off-by-one lag here.

latest_findings.claim: At N=256 and e in [0, 0.5] (seeds 62-64), accel_step crosses the persistent 0.1 margin bar at steps 100, 100 and 110 and reaches half its final margin at steps 90, 100 and 110. The matched N=64 arm crossed the 0.1 bar at steps 90-100, so the N=256 delay is only 0-20 steps, not the >=20 steps in every seed that the hypothesis predicted. The half-final delay is +30 for seed 62 (90 vs 60) but only +10 for seed 63 (100 vs 90). Final accel_step R2 is 0.862-0.883 against controls of 0.674-0.705 (margins 0.177-0.187, all at layer 4). Force does not beat its control at the end (R2 0.18-0.59, margins 0.004-0.030) after an early transient margin of 0.145-0.165 at steps 10-20 that fades to about 0 by step 110. val_mse_ratio is 12.0-13.3, so no seed beats the baseline.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The expected-if-true outcome failed: the 0.1-bar gap is at most 20 steps and is below 20 in at least two seeds, so the seeds 56-58 result (+20/+70/+30) did not replicate cleanly. The expected-if-false outcome (half-final gap <= 10 in at least 2 of 3 seeds) is met only by seed 63; seed 62 is +30. Seed 64's N=64 half-final step was not available to me (the N=64 finding file could not be read). If it is >= 100, the gap is <= 10 and the verdict becomes refuted; otherwise the result stays mixed. The N=64 values here come from summaries quoted in the open questions, not from per-seed trajectories, so the paired differences should be recomputed from the N=64 trajectories. The control-ceiling explanation does not fit this pair: N=256 final margins (0.177-0.187) are higher than the N=64 margins (0.144-0.160 in seeds 62-63), yet N=256 still crosses no earlier. Checkpoints are 10 steps apart, so differences of 10 steps are at the resolution limit. All three N=256 runs completed (300/300 steps), and formed_at_step matches the trajectory in every run.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-045953-52c8 (issue 1): Accepted. Seed 64's N=64 half-final step was available in run-20261012-043022-144a: final margin 0.1672, half is 0.0836, first reached at step 80. That makes seed 64's half-final gap +30 (110 vs 80), not a possible <= 10, so the 'refuted' branch in the confidence note is ruled out. Recomputed from the trajectories, the paired gaps for seeds 62/63/64 are 0/0/+20 on the 0.1 bar, which fails expected_if_true, and +30/+10/+30 on half-final. expected_if_false (half-final <= 10 in 2 of 3) is met only by seed 63, so it is not met. Inconclusive stands, and the status is unchanged. Pooled over the six matched seeds (56-58, 62-64), the mean delay is about +22 on both measures, but per-seed spread on the 0.1 bar is large. This cycle's matched N=64/N=256 pair on seeds 65-69 (5-step checkpoints, pooled 11-seed rule, all values read from run trajectories) resolves it. On the read failure: I can't inspect the pipeline from here, so I've filed it as a new question for whoever maintains the analysis step. Both arms this cycle pre-register reading the formation steps from the per-checkpoint trajectories in the run records.
